QF.id: IV Introduction to Interest Rate Derivatives_3

question.text: In the OTC interest rate derivatives market globally, as per the BIS table cited on p.97 of the NISM Series IV workbook for 2024-S2, the notional amount outstanding for interest rate contracts was closest to:

explanation.text: The Logic: The BIS table on p.97 of NISM Series IV shows OTC interest rate contracts at USD 548,341 billion (about USD 548 trillion) in 2024-S2 and USD 578,805 billion (about USD 579 trillion) in 2024-S1. The closest value among the four options is USD 548 trillion (option D). The Trap: USD 100 billion and USD 1 trillion vastly understate the size of the market. USD 100 trillion is also too low. In the original ambiguous version the stem asked what the amount "exceeds", and the four options were USD 100 billion, USD 1 trillion, USD 100 trillion and USD 500 trillion - the actual figure exceeds ALL of the first three thresholds as well, so any of those options was technically correct. Replacing the threshold framing with "closest to" and using the precise USD 548 trillion figure removes the ambiguity. Note: The original question was ambiguous because an "exceeds" framing made multiple lower thresholds correct simultaneously. The stem has been reworded as a "closest to" question anchored to the BIS 2024-S2 figure on p.97, and the keyed value updated to USD 548 trillion so it is uniquely correct. Source: NISM Series IV, Dec 2025, p.97.
